title: FACT CHECK: VP Sara’s counsel did not call for ‘People Power’ at ASEAN Summit
summary: The quote card attributes a call for mass action to lawyer Sheila Sison, Vice President Sara Duterte's lead counsel, but she did not make such a statement, contrary to the claim

blocks.text: Claim: Lawyer Sheila Sison, lead defense counsel in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, called for “People Power” during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit to expose corruption and humiliate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
Why we fact-checked this: A video was posted on November 14 by the Facebook page Jay Halago Near, a day before the Philippines began hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit.
Its thumbnail carries a quote attributed to Sison, which says, “People Power sa ASEAN Summit! Para malaman ng mundo ang korapsyon sa Pinas, ipapahiya natin si PBBM!”
(People Power at the ASEAN Summit! So the world will know about corruption in the Philippines, we will humiliate [President Bongbong Marcos]!)
The graphic has a “PH News Update” label and the word “Korapsyon? (Corruption?)” beside a photo of Marcos.

The post’s caption reads: “People Power sa ASEAN Summit? Panawagan laban sa korapsyon, umani ng atensyon! Dapat bang gawing pagkakataon ang ASEAN Summit para iparinig ang hinaing ng taumbayan? Kayo, anong opinyon ninyo?”
(People Power at the ASEAN Summit? A call against corruption draws attention! Should the ASEAN Summit be used to air the people’s grievances? What is your opinion?)
As of writing, the video has 93,000 views, 5,900 reactions, 1,700 comments, and 758 shares.
The facts: No news report or public statement shows Sison urging the public to gather for a “people power” movement during the ASEAN Summit.
Sison is lead defense counsel in Duterte’s ongoing impeachment trial, and her recent public remarks concern the case.

On November 10, she raised concerns before the impeachment court over statements that private prosecutors made to the media. On November 12, she asked the court to cancel the November 13 session. None of these accounts mentions the ASEAN Summit or any call for mass action.

Protest amid ASEAN: Protests did take place during the summit, but Sison did not lead them, and they were not a People Power call to humiliate Marcos over government corruption. On November 15, the summit’s opening day, police clashed with activists at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila as they attempted to march toward the summit venue.

Groups under Bagong Alyansang Makabayan and the All Workers Unity coalition were protesting antiworker policies, the arrival of US President Donald Trump, and the proposed Pax Silica hub in New Clark City.

Police said the groups lacked a permit to assemble outside the Freedom Park. Nearly 300 arrests were made in Muntinlupa alone following the protests. (READ: Lawmakers, groups slam November 15 arrests: Where is maximum tolerance?)
The Palace has previously urged protesters not to “tarnish” the country’s reputation during the summit.
The Philippines, ASEAN chair for 2026, is hosting the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17. (LIVE UPDATES: 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila)

Impeachment trial: Meanwhile, Duterte’s impeachment trial continues. By the end of its 43rd day on November 12, the trial examined two major credit card purchases by the Vice President’s husband, Manases Carpio, in Japan and Malaysia, with witnesses explaining the expenses as shared dining and purchases for basketball players.
Rappler has fact-checked similar claims related to the impeachment trial.
